LEARN VOID / CONCURRENCY

Task groups & cancellation

Give related work a lifetime.

Async execution

This example uses the explicit async host adapter. Its source is checked by the compiler; it is not a synchronous CLI entry program.

Keep child work with its parent

Every async activation owns a child scope. with tasks.group() as jobs creates an explicit nested scope. Normal group exit waits for its children; dropping a task handle does not detach the task.

Handle early exits deliberately

An early exit from a nested scope requests cancellation of unfinished work and waits for it to settle. cancel() is cooperative and idempotent. Cleanup runs for code that was actually reached; cancellation is not a recoverable Err value.

Read the lifecycle example

The program exercises normal completion, repeated awaits, cancellation and early returns. Its checks return small error codes if a lifecycle expectation is broken. With input 5, the successful path returns 6. It requires the explicit async host adapter.
